Pico 2 W keyboard bridge (legacy, unused)

This fork does not use the Pico. The host does not start this bridge and does not
listen on port 39381. Follow README.md in the project root and enter the
bootstrap launch commands manually. These notes are retained for reference only.

The configured Pico needs no update for this cleanup. Its pairing key is preserved
in smilebasic/pico-keyboard/secret. Keep the PC and console on the same network.

START
1. Open fresh SmileBASIC Direct mode.
2. Run ./start.sh from the project root and choose the computer address on
   the console's network.
3. Reconnect the Pico to the Switch with GP0 and GP1 ungrounded.
   It loads NS2 and types the fresh connection command.
4. Keep the PC host running. After a failed native session, restart the console
   before retrying. REMOVE must only run once per application process.

INITIAL INSTALL / NETWORK CHANGE
Ground GP0 to GND and connect the Pico to the PC without holding BOOTSEL.
Run from the project root:
  bash smilebasic/pico-keyboard/install.sh /path/to/CIRCUITPY computer-IP
The installer asks for Wi-Fi credentials and installs the keyboard code,
bootstrap as program.bas, and HID library. Unplug and remove the GP0 jumper.
Use English (US) for the Switch USB keyboard language.

To enter the BASIC bootstrap for the first time, focus an empty EDIT0 editor
and connect with GP1 grounded. It types program.bas; save the result as NS2.
The source of truth is smilebasic/bootstrap.bas.
